title: Benchmark fused HNF storage reuse
objective: Implement an isolated frozen vector429 128x64 HNF A/B benchmark comparing 32 fresh prefix calls with a fused retained-storage candidate, exact prefix/final oracles, allocation metrics, and pinned alternating timings
references: vector429 p=2 OM mixed-radix quotient lattice

oracles: Exact equality of every two-row prefix HNF and final HNF

handoff.summary: Added an isolated, reproducible A/B benchmark for the authentic vector429 p=2 128x64 mixed-quotient HNF. The benchmark freezes the exact input and final HNF, proves the final lattice equals the independent PARI local lattice, compares every one of 32 two-row prefix HNFs exactly, accounts for logical buffer/materialization traffic, and measures seven pinned alternating pairs. Keeping exact storage resident in one native call reduced mean time from 3.4153 s to 0.5210 s (6.555x), native calls from 32 to 1, and IntegerBuffer constructions from 96 to 3.
risks: This is one deliberately selected authentic degree-64 HNF workload, so the 6.555x ratio must not be generalized to every HNF shape.
Materialization figures are exact wrapper-level logical counts and requested buffer capacities, not allocator hooks, malloc counts, or peak RSS.
The production fused kernel already existed at the lane base; this lane adds frozen evidence and no production implementation change.
next_steps: Use the same validate-once, retain-exact-storage, publish-once structure around the next multi-stage exact class-group workflow.
If allocator behavior itself becomes the question, add native allocator telemetry separately instead of interpreting logical capacity as physical allocation.
